newIsolated.value: In this chapter Admit a corpus bundle only when an independently selected provenance record and every supplied payload agree, without making retrieval or storage layout part of the content rules.
Terms for connecting selected corpus bytes to provenance and keeping content checks separate from retrieval and storage.

Quick reference A verified corpus bundle Terms for connecting selected corpus bytes to provenance and keeping content checks separate from retrieval and storage. Canonical manifest A complete corpus record with one fixed byte representation, including content IDs, roles, counts, digests and provenance. The verifier rejects different formatting or ordering rather than silently rewriting it. Content ID A logical name for one payload in the selected corpus record. A source uses that name to refer to content; adapters choose how to retrieve or store it. The name is not a required filename or URL. Corpus bundle The selected raw text and metadata payloads together with their manifest. In this synthetic example, two sources share one license payload and one attribution payload. Dataset artifact identity The SHA-256 digest of the complete canonical manifest. It identifies the record through its provenance and payload digests; supplied payload bytes still need verification. It is not a signature or permission certificate. Raw held-out source The separate raw text source selected outside the raw training source. Its name does not define the final validation or test split, which is constructed later. Source provenance The record connecting selected corpus content to its source revision, provenance reference, license text and attribution. Matching those claims does not establish that they are true or grant permission.

Reproduce the same-size corruption and explain why its length passes but its content is refused. COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \ -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \ --test governed_acquisition \ size_digest_truncation_and_overrun_are_separate_failures -- --exact

Reproduce the attribution-only variant. Identify which payload entry changes and which source references remain unchanged. COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \ -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \ --test governed_acquisition \ provenance_changes_identity_without_changing_raw_digests -- --exact

Reproduce verification and storage failures. Explain why a private candidate does not replace the last successfully published memory bundle. COURSE_CORPUS=false ./course run cargo test --offline --locked \ -p ch41-governed-corpus-acquisition \ --test governed_acquisition \ failure_preserves_prior_bundle_without_publishing_partial_candidate -- --exact
Both abc and abd contain 3 bytes, but their digests differ. The selected entry expects the digest of abc; the verifier returns Hash for abd instead of admitting it as the selected content.

Only the attribution payload entry’s count and digest change. Both sources still refer to content ID attribution, and the raw text entries keep their original digests. The changed canonical manifest changes the identity. The variant needs its own independently selected policy.

The test injects a corrupt final payload and separate write, finish and publication failures. In each case the memory store keeps the prior bundle and publishes no replacement. Earlier verified payloads remain in private staging, not in a partially admitted bundle. This is the tested memory-store boundary, not a guarantee of crash recovery for arbitrary storage.

Verify a corpus together with its provenance Verify selected corpus bytes and source provenance as one complete bundle, independently of retrieval and storage, using a small offline Rust example. Content revision: 4
